jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
**The Opportunity**

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is a newly created executive role at The Open Door Network — and one of the most consequential hires the organization will make. TODN is a Bakersfield\-based nonprofit with over 200 employees supporting victim advocacy, homeless services, trauma\-informed care, medical respite, workforce development, childcare, and clinical services across multiple sites, including a new four\-building shelter campus at 529 Dolores Street.

Reporting directly to the CEO, the COO will own the internal operational leadership of the organization — overseeing programs and grants and data — so the CEO can remain focused on external strategy, board governance, the capital campaign, and community relationships.

This is a hands\-on executive role for a seasoned operator who thrives in complex, mission\-driven environments. The COO will serve as a trusted operational partner to the CEO, building the systems, structures, and accountability culture TODN needs to sustain and accelerate its growth.

**What You’ll Do**

**Operational Leadership**

● Provide day\-to\-day executive oversight of TODN’s program and grants functions

● Partner closely with the CEO to advance organizational priorities, taking ownership of internal operations so the CEO can remain focused on external leadership and mission growth

● Build and maintain a culture of accountability, transparency, and high performance across all departments

● Lead cross\-functional coordination to eliminate silos and ensure alignment across a multi\-site, multi\-program organization

● Represent the CEO internally and with key operational partners as delegated

● Willingness to work evenings and weekends as needed to attend internal and external events, community functions, and organizational activities

**Programs Oversight**

● Supervise the Director of Programs and provide strategic and operational guidance across TODN’s full service continuum: victim advocacy, homeless services, trauma\-informed care, medical respite, workforce development, childcare, and clinical services

● Ensure programs are delivered with fidelity, meet contractual and grant compliance requirements, and are staffed appropriately

● Lead operational planning for the Dolores Street four\-building shelter campus, including on\-campus service model design, vendor coordination, and readiness milestones

● Partner with program directors to develop and monitor performance metrics, client outcome data, and program quality indicators

**Grants \& Compliance**

● Supervise the Director of Grants \& Data and ensure organizational compliance with all federal, state, and private grant requirements

● Maintain working fluency in 2 CFR 200 Uniform Guidance; ensure TODN’s grant management practices meet audit standards

● Partner with the Controller and CEO on financial reporting obligations tied to grant awards

● Oversee the development and maintenance of internal controls, policies, and documentation systems that support grant compliance and organizational integrity

● Support grant renewals, reports, and new funding applications in coordination with the grants team and CEO

**Strategy \& Organizational Development**

● Translate the CEO’s strategic vision and board direction into operational plans, timelines, and accountability structures

● Lead implementation of TODN’s strategic planning priorities using a quarterly planning and tracking system

● Lead a structural review of TODN’s organizational design — assessing reporting lines, spans of control, role clarity, and departmental alignment — and present findings and recommendations to the CEO and board

● Design and build organizational infrastructure — SOPs, internal controls, workflows, and systems — that supports sustainable scale

● Identify operational risks and lead mitigation planning; escalate board\-level issues to the CEO in a timely manner

● Support the CEO in board reporting by preparing operational updates, metrics dashboards, and risk summaries

**What We’re Looking For**

**You’ll thrive in this role if you:**

● Bring 7–12 years of progressive leadership in nonprofit, government, or human services operations, with demonstrated experience managing multi\-department or multi\-program organizations at comparable scale (150\+ staff preferred)

● Have strong working knowledge of federal grant compliance, including 2 CFR 200 Uniform Guidance, and a proven track record building and supervising senior\-level teams

● Have experience developing and implementing organizational infrastructure, SOPs, and internal controls

● Are an exceptional organizer and project manager — able to hold multiple complex workstreams simultaneously without losing momentum or detail

● Lead with high emotional intelligence; able to hold authority with compassion in a trauma\-informed environment where staff carry significant vicarious burden

● Interest to represent the organization at community events, government hearings, and other external stakeholder functions

● Communicate clearly and confidently in writing and in person, including with boards and external stakeholders

● Graduate degree in public administration, nonprofit management, social work, business, or related field

**Preferred**

● Background in human services, trauma\-informed care, housing, or behavioral health, with experience in homeless services or victim advocacy program management

● Familiarity with California nonprofit compliance requirements and California human resources laws

● Prior experience managing a capital project, facility expansion, or new site launch

● Kern County or Central Valley networks and community ties

**Compensation \& Benefits**

● Salary: $120,000 – $150,000 annually, commensurate with experience

● Comprehensive medical insurance for eligible employees and their dependents, effective the first day of the month following 30 days of continuous employment

● Dental and vision insurance

● 401(k) retirement

**THE ORGANIZATION:**
The San Luis \& Delta\-Mendota Water Authority was established in January of 1992 and consists of 27 member agencies providing water service to approximately 1,200,000 acres of irrigated agriculture, 2 million people, and 130,000 acres of wetlands within the western San Joaquin Valley, San Benito and Santa Clara counties.  

One of the primary purposes of establishing the Authority was to assume the operation and maintenance (O\&M) responsibilities of certain United States Bureau of Reclamation (USBR) Central Valley Project facilities at an optimum level. **FACILITIES \& OPERATIONS:**
Authority facilities include the C.W. “Bill” Jones Pumping Plant, Delta\-Mendota Canal, O’Neill Pumping/Generation Plant, San Luis Drain, Delta Cross Channel, Tracy Fish Collection Facility, and the Delta\-Mendota Canal\-California Aqueduct Intertie. **THE ROLE:*****A senior executive role at the intersection of infrastructure, public service, organizational leadership, and California water.***  

The COO is an executive leader responsible for operational performance, organizational alignment, and effective execution of Capital Projects across the Authority.  

The COO reports directly to the Executive Director and directs Operations \& Maintenance, Engineering, Procurement, Capital Improvement Projects, Control Operations and Safety.  

The COO is responsible and accountable for the planning, management, performance, and improvement of the Authority’s O\&M and Capital Improvement Project functions. As a key member of the executive leadership team, the COO represents the Executive Director in interactions with employees, the public, member agencies, and other organizations.  

The COO will work in Tracy with a regular presence in Los Banos for Committee and Board Meetings and time at other Authority locations as needed. **LEADERSHIP PRIORITIES:*** Provide executive direction for administration of the O\&M Transfer Agreement with the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation for Transferred Works facilities.
* Lead development, preparation, and administration of the annual budget, including fiscal analysis and review of budget proposals and requests.
* Provide direction and leadership for O\&M staff and ensure the Authority’s safety practices and programs are coordinated, implemented, and maintained.
* Coordinate activities across departments to promote a high level of organizational and program efficiency.
* Work closely with the Executive Director on strategic planning, implementation plans, priorities, and Authority policy development.
* Represent the Executive Director before federal, state, and local agencies and other organizations.
* Support Board of Directors meetings, information flow, and coordination among member agencies.
* Oversee Capital Improvement Projects, special studies and evaluations of Authority programs and services and communicate established Board policies effectively.

SLDMWA seeks an accomplished leader who combines sound judgment, operational discipline, strong communication, and the ability to build trusted relationships.  

The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated ability to identify creative, practical solutions to complex problems and the determination to see them through. The ability to approach difficult challenges with confidence, remove obstacles to progress, and ensure the Water Authority successfully fulfills its responsibility to deliver safe, clean, and reliable water to its members. **EDUCATION \& EXPERIENCE:**
Any combination of education and experience that provides the necessary knowledge and abilities may be qualifying. A typical path includes a bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in engineering, public administration, business administration, or a related field, together with ten years of supervisory, management, or executive experience.  

Broad management experience in a public agency, including responsibility for program formulation and implementation and the management of administrative operations, is preferred. **WHAT SUCCESS REQUIRES:*** Executive leadership in a public\-agency environment, including governance, strategic planning, performance management, policy development, and continuous improvement.
* Strong people leadership: selecting, motivating, developing, supervising, and constructively evaluating managers and staff.
* Knowledge of water\-agency operations, including operation and maintenance of major infrastructure, asset management, and capital construction.
* Working knowledge of laws, regulations, legal mandates, guidelines, and standards affecting public agencies, particularly water agencies.
* Ability to establish goals, objectives, policies, procedures, work standards, and internal controls—and to translate them into effective execution.
* Ability to balance competing objectives, negotiate effective resolutions, and maintain discretion and integrity with sensitive information.
* Excellent written and oral communication skills and the ability to build cooperative relationships with member agencies, public agencies, staff, and the public.
* Ability to manage complex, multi\-team projects requiring coordination with external agencies and senior executives.

The Northeast Community Clinics, a growing Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) with 18 locations serving many parts of Los Angeles County, is recruiting its next Director of Operations/COO.

For almost 50 years, Northeast Community Clinics (NECC) has been providing comprehensive, culturally competent, high quality primary health and a wide variety of specialty care throughout Los Angeles for diverse, underserved communities, regardless of the patients’ financial status.

The range of services provided by the NECC include: Pediatric, prenatal, family planning, adult general medicine, dental, optometry, endocrinology, and 24\-hour emergency coverage through on\-call physicians.

With a growing budget of $54M and over 400 employees, NECC serves more than 45,000 patients annually.

Due to a number of current initiatives, including the integration of two physician practices, launching of a Program of All\-Inclusive Care for the Elderly (PACE), new contracts and grants and other programs addressing emerging social determinants of health, NECC is poised for continued acceleration of growth in resources and programs for the communities they serve.

Reporting to the Executive Director/CEO, the Operations Director/Chief Operating Officer is a key and influential member of executive management, responsible for the establishment and implementation of policies and procedures across the organization designed to promote optimal quality, efficiency, profitability and productivity.

**Program Overview**
The 49ers STEM Leadership Institute (SLI), created in partnership with the San Francisco 49ers, Silicon Valley Education Foundation (SVEF), and the Santa Clara Unified School District (SCUSD), is a six\-year program that will prepare students with high academic potential to be outstanding.


SLI began in Summer 2014 with a cohort of 60 incoming seventh grade students. A new cohort of 60 incoming seventh graders is selected through a competitive application process each year, and students advance with their cohort to the next grade level. By the end of the six\-year rollout process, there will be a total of 360 students from grades 7 – 12 involved in the program, located at two state of the art digital fabrication labs at Cabrillo Middle School and Santa Clara High School in the Santa Clara Unified School District. Students complete a rigorous college preparatory curriculum, engage in STEM projects and competitions, and participate annually in 300\+ hours of additional learning time.### **Program Director – 49ers STEM Leadership Institute**


Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer (COO) at Silicon Valley Education Foundation (SVEF), the Program Director provides strategic, operational, and programmatic leadership for the 49ers STEM Leadership Institute (SLI). The Director oversees the program in its entirety across grades 7–12 and works closely with SVEF leadership, Program Managers, Program Coordinator, SCUSD administrators and teaching staff, the 49ers Foundation, corporate and university partners, students, and families.


The Program Director serves as the central point connecting the many organizations and individuals involved in SLI and is responsible for ensuring that the program remains student\-centered, operationally strong, financially sustainable, innovative, and aligned with the goals of SVEF, SCUSD, and the 49ers Foundation.

* Identify emerging STEM, technology, education, and workforce trends and determine how they should influence SLI programming.
* Contribute to SVEF organizational strategic planning and represent the needs, opportunities, and priorities of SLI.

* Oversee the day\-to\-day operation of the entire SLI program across middle and high school.
* Develop and maintain sustainable policies, SOPs, workflows, calendars, systems, and accountability structures.
* Coordinate school\-year programming, Extended Hours, Open Lab, workshops, field experiences, competitions, showcases, partner programs, and special initiatives.
* Ensure FabLab operations, equipment access, safety expectations, training, scheduling, materials, and replenishment support program needs.
* Identify operational risks and resolve issues before they significantly affect students, families, teachers, or partners.
* Ensure institutional knowledge and critical processes are documented rather than dependent on individual staff members.

**Team Leadership \& Staff Development**

* Lead and support Program Managers, Program Coordinator, and other program staff.
* Establish clear responsibilities, priorities, deliverables, and expectations.
* Conduct regular team meetings, individual check\-ins, coaching, performance reviews, and professional development.
* Delegate program ownership while maintaining appropriate accountability and oversight.
* Identify staffing needs and participate in recruitment, hiring, onboarding, training, and succession planning.

**Stewardship: Honor the legacy. Invest in the future.**

* Provide overall leadership, vision, and operational direction for the venue in alignment with 415 Presents’ mission, core values, and strategic pillars for Curran Theatre.

* Achieves annual fundraising goals across major gifts, annual giving, grateful patient giving, planned giving, corporate and foundation relations, and special initiatives.

Bachelor's Degree Related Field of Study required or Master's Degree Related Field of Study preferred.

Executive Director. Reports to: Board of Directors as a whole. Supervisory responsibility: all employees, directly or through designated supervisors; oversight of contractors and professional advisers within approved agreements. The President is the ordinary Board liaison, not a substitute for collective Board authority.

FLSA classification: Exempt only while the actual duties, salary basis, and applicable salary requirements meet a lawful executive or administrative exemption. CHWW shall document and communicate the classification under Handbook Section 1\.C. In the absence of a documented valid exemption, the position is nonexempt and all compensable time must be recorded and paid.

Position Summary

The Executive Director is CHWW's chief employed administrator and is accountable for the overall management, financial stability, safe and reliable water service, personnel, regulatory coordination, member service, and execution of Board policy. In a small rural utility, the role includes both management and hands\-on administrative work, filling reasonable operational gaps, and developing dependable backup systems. The Executive Director is expected to anticipate needs, bring material issues to the Board early, and obtain appropriate professional assistance rather than perform unlicensed work or assume unrestricted authority.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

1\. Leadership, planning, and daily administration. Translate the mission and Board decisions into work priorities, procedures, budgets, and measurable objectives. Coordinate treatment, distribution, billing, customer service, finance, HR, technology, and administrative functions. Resolve cross\-department issues; assign work; monitor completion; and maintain continuity when staffing is limited. Recommend organizational improvements and sustainable service standards.

2\. Board and corporate governance. Prepare agendas, management reports, budgets, proposed policies, and decision materials with the President and Secretary\-Treasurer. Present accurate operational, financial, compliance, personnel, and risk information without obscuring adverse developments. Support meeting notices, elections, membership records, minutes, corporate filings, and required member communications while preserving the Secretary\-Treasurer's accountability. Implement approved actions and maintain an action\-item record. Obtain counsel's advice on governing documents, records requests, open\-government applicability, major transactions, and disputed authority. Maintain a current governing\-document and amendment register, distinguish charter requirements from ordinary bylaw quorum rules, and obtain legal review of election terms and adoption thresholds. Maintain complete approval records for each election, amendment, and corporate action.

3\. Financial stewardship. Develop annual operating and capital budgets and multiyear financial and asset\-replacement plans. Monitor revenue, cash flow, costs, reserves, debt service, covenant compliance, and budget variances. Coordinate bookkeeping, payroll, tax filings, financial statements, and the independent annual audit with qualified staff and advisers. Recommend rates, fees, deposits, and financial policies to the Board with supporting cost and affordability information; implement only lawfully adopted changes. Ensure invoices and payroll are accurate and timely, and maintain independent approval and reconciliation controls even when personally covering financial tasks.

4\. Funding, grants, and lender relations. Identify suitable financing, grants, technical assistance, and reimbursement opportunities. Coordinate applications, feasibility information, matching resources, environmental and procurement conditions, reporting, draw requests, and closeout. Track restricted funds and avoid commitments before required approval. Maintain productive relationships with lenders, grant administrators, and financial advisers. Do not promise funding or eligibility before verification or incur debt outside Board authority.

5\. Drinking\-water and environmental compliance. Maintain a complete register of the utility's facilities, permits, operating conditions, sampling and reporting duties, inspection findings, and renewal dates. Ensure adequate licensed treatment and distribution staffing and backup coverage appropriate to each system classification. Coordinate compliance with the Safe Drinking Water Act, applicable Florida DEP and other public\-health requirements, Northwest Florida Water Management District requirements, and other applicable authorities. Require qualified review of sampling, operational logs, consumer confidence reports, public notices, water\-use reports, cross\-connection control, and corrective actions. Track applicable lead and copper, PFAS, and other rule changes with qualified advisers, identifying each adopted requirement and its effective date. Oversee continuing service\-line inventory verification, updates, customer notices, replacement planning, and related funding documentation. Maintain current compliance and funding records.

6\. Operations and infrastructure. Oversee source\-water availability, treatment, storage, distribution pressure, water quality, metering, asset condition, preventive maintenance, inventory, fleet readiness, and water\-loss control through qualified staff. Review work orders, outages, repairs, inspections, alarm response, and maintenance backlogs. Plan timely replacement or expansion of wells, tanks, mains, pumps, controls, and other assets. Ensure current maps and asset records, physical security, appropriate easements and access, and reliable supply and repair arrangements. Do not promise fire\-flow capacity, system extensions, or new connections without technical and legal verification. United Way of the Plains’ mission is “To improve lives by harnessing the caring power of our community to advance the common good in south central Kansas.” Since 1922, we have brought together individuals and organizations to create real and lasting results. We serve Sedgwick, Butler, Cowley, Sumner and surrounding counties in south central Kansas, covering approximately 800,000 people. We bring individuals and organizations together to meet the biggest needs in our community in innovative ways. We do this by forging unlikely partnerships, forming new solutions to old problems and mobilizing the best ideas and resources. But we don’t do it alone. We inspire others to join the fight. We enable individuals, groups and companies to make a difference – individually and collectively – through their time, talents and treasure.



United Way of the Plains goes beyond just funding programs. We conduct research and look for ways to address specific issues through coordinated efforts, called collective impact. Join a Team Making a Lasting Impact in Northern Kent County



North Kent Connect (NKC) is a Christian organization committed to improving the lives of all people in northern Kent County by providing access to basic needs and promoting economic independence.



As an organization running the Entrepreneurial Operating System (EOS®), we operate with vision, accountability, and healthy communication at every level. Our team is aligned, empowered, and passionate about our mission: every person has value.



At NKC, our core values are at the heart of everything we do:


* People First We treat everyone with respect and kindness, offering fantastic service and genuine care.
* Dynamic We are passionate, proactive, and resourceful, always finding creative ways to move our vision forward.
* Aligned We are united toward a common goal, working collaboratively with a spirit of camaraderie and fun.


Our niche is simple yet powerful: we go beyond basic needs. We connect people to resources that help them move forward and thrive. As the only organization of its kind in northern Kent County, we offer a unique blend of expertise, services, and community partnerships.



When you visit NKC, you’ll be met with professionalism, follow\-through, and a team that lives out its values every day. We're passionate about what we do, clear on where we’re going, and we have a lot of fun along the way.

North Kent Connect is seeking a strategic, relationship\-driven Director of Development to lead the organization's fund development strategy and deepen engagement with the donors, volunteers, businesses, churches, foundations, and community partners who make our mission possible.



The Director of Development is a key organizational leader responsible for building and executing a comprehensive development strategy that strengthens NKC's long\-term sustainability. Working closely with the Executive Director and Leadership Team, this position will identify opportunities to grow philanthropic support, cultivate meaningful donor relationships, strengthen community engagement, and ensure NKC communicates its mission and impact effectively.



This role is for someone who sees development as more than fundraising. It's about building relationships, connecting people to purpose, and creating opportunities for the community to invest their time, talent, and treasure in NKC's mission.

Our ideal candidate will be a strategic thinker, strong relationship builder, engaging communicator, and collaborative leader who is passionate about NKC's mission and will:



1\. Embody the Three Core Values of NKC \|

* People First: Treat everyone with respect; be helpful and kind; provide fantastic service.
* Dynamic: Be passionate about the mission, enthusiastic, proactive, and resourceful.
* Aligned: Work united toward a common goal with collaboration, camaraderie, and fun.


2\. Lead Development Strategy \| Develop and execute a comprehensive fund development strategy aligned with NKC's strategic priorities and long\-term financial sustainability.
